text: With EQUAL leak rates α at every layer, how does the effective time constant at layer ℓ scale with depth?
choices: τ^(ℓ) ≈ ℓ / α  (grows linearly with depth)
τ^(ℓ) ≈ 1 / α  (the same at every layer)
explanation: For equal α the layer-ℓ impulse response is a negative-binomial (Pascal) kernel whose center of mass is ≈ ℓ/α, so the time constant grows LINEARLY with depth (an arithmetic hierarchy). Option 3 ignores the deepening memory. Exponential growth (option 2) requires geometrically DECREASING leak rates α_ℓ = α_1 r^(ℓ−1), not equal rates. Option 0 has the dependence backwards.
